paragraphs.title: Jacob Gathers His Sons for Prophecy

easy.question: Whom did Jacob call?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Jacob called unto his sons.”

easy.question: What did Jacob ask his sons to do?
easy.explanation: Jacob told them to gather together and hear his words.

easy.question: What did Jacob want to tell his sons about?
answers: What would happen to them in the future
easy.explanation: He would tell them what would befall them in the last days.

medium.question: Why did Jacob ask his sons to gather and listen?
answers: To tell them important things about their future
medium.explanation: Jacob gathered them to tell them what would happen in the future.

medium.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: The sons listened, then Jacob called them
Jacob called his sons, asked them to gather, and told them to listen
Jacob left, then the sons gathered
medium.explanation: First Jacob called them, then asked them to gather, and finally told them to hear.

medium.question: What does “in the last days” mean here?
answers: The future or a later time
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to events that would happen later.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Jacob repeating the idea of listening?
answers: He did not want them to understand
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that his sons should listen carefully.

challenge.question: Why do the verses use both the names “Jacob” and “Israel”?
answers: Both are names of the same father
challenge.explanation: Jacob and Israel are names for the same man.

challenge.question: What does “what shall befall you” show about Jacob’s message?
answers: It concerns what will happen to his sons
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the sons’ future.

questions.question: What can we infer from Jacob repeating the idea of listening?
answers: He did not want them to understand
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that his sons should listen carefully.

questions.question: Why do the verses use both the names “Jacob” and “Israel”?
answers: Both are names of the same father
questions.explanation: Jacob and Israel are names for the same man.

questions.question: What does “what shall befall you” show about Jacob’s message?
answers: It concerns what will happen to his sons
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the sons’ future.

easy.question: To whom does Jacob first speak?
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Reuben, thou art my firstborn.”

easy.question: What was Reuben’s status?
easy.explanation: Jacob calls Reuben his firstborn.

easy.question: What is Reuben’s behavior compared to?
easy.explanation: Jacob says, “Unstable as water.”

medium.question: Why would Reuben not retain the advantage of the firstborn?
answers: He went up to his father’s bed and defiled it
medium.explanation: He lost his status because he dishonored his father’s bed.

medium.question: What does “unstable” mean in “Unstable as water”?
medium.explanation: Water suggests instability and a lack of firmness.

medium.question: How do verses 3 and 4 relate?
answers: Verse 4 explains why Reuben became king
Verse 3 states Reuben’s advantages, and verse 4 explains why he lost them
medium.explanation: His birthright and strength are followed by the reason he lost his special position.

challenge.question: What is the main contrast in Jacob’s words about Reuben?
answers: He had high status as firstborn, but his rash behavior damaged it
He was physically weak but wise
He was young but had a large family
challenge.explanation: Reuben had the advantages of the firstborn, but his impulsive act cost him that position.

challenge.question: What does “then defiledst thou it” mean here?
answers: Reuben dishonored his father by his action
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes Reuben’s dishonoring of his father.

challenge.question: Why is water an appropriate image for Reuben?
answers: Water flows and changes, like unstable behavior
challenge.explanation: The image emphasizes Reuben’s instability and rashness.

questions.question: What is the main contrast in Jacob’s words about Reuben?
answers: He had high status as firstborn, but his rash behavior damaged it
He was physically weak but wise
He was young but had a large family
questions.explanation: Reuben had the advantages of the firstborn, but his impulsive act cost him that position.

questions.question: What does “then defiledst thou it” mean here?
answers: Reuben dishonored his father by his action
questions.explanation: The phrase describes Reuben’s dishonoring of his father.

questions.question: Why is water an appropriate image for Reuben?
answers: Water flows and changes, like unstable behavior
questions.explanation: The image emphasizes Reuben’s instability and rashness.

paragraphs.title: Simeon and Levi and the Power of Anger

easy.question: Who are mentioned together at the beginning?
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Simeon and Levi are brethren.”

easy.question: How is their anger described?
easy.explanation: Their anger was fierce and their wrath cruel.

easy.question: What would Jacob do to Simeon and Levi?
easy.explanation: Jacob says he will divide them and scatter them in Israel.

medium.question: Why does Jacob reject their secret and assembly?
medium.explanation: Jacob rejects them because of their violent actions.

medium.question: What were the “instruments of cruelty” in this passage?
medium.explanation: The context identifies them as instruments used for violence.

medium.question: How are their actions connected to Jacob’s decision?
answers: Because of their anger and violence, Jacob said they would be scattered
Because they were righteous, Jacob gave them the land
Because they were weak, Jacob sent them to study
medium.explanation: Their violence led Jacob to announce their division and scattering.

challenge.question: What does Jacob curse in verse 7?
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “Cursed be their anger” and “their wrath.”

challenge.question: What can we infer from “mine honour, be not thou united” with their assembly?
answers: Jacob does not want to identify with their actions
Jacob wants to join their actions
challenge.explanation: Jacob refuses to associate his honor with their assembly.

challenge.question: What idea connects “instruments of cruelty” and “cursed be their anger”?
answers: Their violence came from intense anger, which Jacob condemned
challenge.explanation: Both phrases emphasize their violent anger.

questions.question: What does Jacob curse in verse 7?
questions.explanation: The verse says, “Cursed be their anger” and “their wrath.”

questions.question: What can we infer from “mine honour, be not thou united” with their assembly?
answers: Jacob does not want to identify with their actions
Jacob wants to join their actions
questions.explanation: Jacob refuses to associate his honor with their assembly.

questions.question: What idea connects “instruments of cruelty” and “cursed be their anger”?
answers: Their violence came from intense anger, which Jacob condemned
questions.explanation: Both phrases emphasize their violent anger.

easy.question: To whom are these words spoken?
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Judah, thou art he.”

easy.question: What would Judah’s brothers do?
easy.explanation: His father’s children would bow before him.

easy.question: What animal is Judah compared to?
easy.explanation: Judah is called a lion’s whelp and a lion.

medium.question: What does “thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies” mean?
medium.explanation: The image of a hand on an enemy’s neck represents victory.

medium.question: What sequence of ideas appears in these verses?
answers: Judah receives honor, is compared to a lion, and is described as a ruler
The nations first submit, then Judah becomes weak
medium.explanation: The passage moves from honor and victory to lion-like strength and lasting rule.

medium.question: What is a “lawgiver” in this context?
answers: A ruler or giver of law
medium.explanation: The context of the scepter and rule identifies a lawgiver as a ruler.

challenge.question: What can we infer from “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”?
challenge.explanation: The scepter represents authority, and “shall not depart” suggests lasting rule.

challenge.question: What does the image of a resting lion that no one can rouse express?
answers: Strength and confidence that cannot be challenged
A need for help from his brothers
challenge.explanation: The resting lion represents power and security.

challenge.question: What does “unto him shall the gathering of the people be” mean?
answers: The nations will hide from him
The nations will fight one another
The nations will gather to him and accept his authority
challenge.explanation: The people will turn to him and recognize his leadership.

questions.question: What can we infer from “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”?
questions.explanation: The scepter represents authority, and “shall not depart” suggests lasting rule.

questions.question: What does the image of a resting lion that no one can rouse express?
answers: Strength and confidence that cannot be challenged
A need for help from his brothers
questions.explanation: The resting lion represents power and security.

questions.question: What does “unto him shall the gathering of the people be” mean?
answers: The nations will hide from him
The nations will fight one another
The nations will gather to him and accept his authority
questions.explanation: The people will turn to him and recognize his leadership.

paragraphs.title: Abundance and Blessing in Judah’s Land

easy.question: To what is the foal tied?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Binding his foal unto the vine.”

easy.question: What is used to wash the garments?
easy.explanation: He washes his garments in wine.

easy.question: What makes the teeth white?
easy.explanation: The verse says his teeth are white with milk.

medium.question: What is described after the foal is tied to the vine?
medium.explanation: The next image is washing garments in wine.

medium.question: What does “binding his foal” describe?
medium.explanation: The phrase describes tying the animal to the vine.

medium.question: What idea is shared by the wine and milk images?
answers: They are used only as medicine
medium.explanation: Both images portray plentiful, valuable produce.

challenge.question: What can we infer from washing garments in wine?
challenge.explanation: The unusual use of wine pictures great abundance.

challenge.question: How do the wine-colored eyes and milk-white teeth relate?
challenge.explanation: Together they create an image of prosperity and well-being.

challenge.question: What does the combination of vine and choice vine emphasize?
answers: The person is leaving the vineyards
There is an abundance of fruitful vines
challenge.explanation: The repeated vineyard imagery reinforces agricultural abundance.

questions.question: What can we infer from washing garments in wine?
questions.explanation: The unusual use of wine pictures great abundance.

questions.question: How do the wine-colored eyes and milk-white teeth relate?
questions.explanation: Together they create an image of prosperity and well-being.

questions.question: What does the combination of vine and choice vine emphasize?
answers: The person is leaving the vineyards
There is an abundance of fruitful vines
questions.explanation: The repeated vineyard imagery reinforces agricultural abundance.

easy.question: Where will Zebulun dwell?
answers: At the haven of the sea
easy.explanation: The verse says Zebulun will dwell at the haven of the sea.

easy.question: What will his haven be associated with?
easy.explanation: He will be a haven of ships.

easy.question: What place is mentioned?
easy.explanation: The verse says his border will be unto Zidon.

medium.question: What can we understand from Zebulun being by the sea and a haven of ships?
answers: His region was connected with the sea and sailing
His region was far from water
He lived only inside a city
medium.explanation: Both phrases emphasize Zebulun’s maritime setting.

medium.question: What does “his border” mean here?
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the boundary extending toward Zidon.

medium.question: What do the words “a haven of ships” add?
answers: They emphasize the connection with ships
They remove the connection with the sea
They describe a place without a shore
medium.explanation: They specify that the coastal area serves ships.

challenge.question: What is a reasonable inference from Zebulun’s being a haven of ships?
answers: He lived only in the mountains
He may have been connected with sailing and sea trade
He was forbidden to approach the sea
challenge.explanation: A harbor could support sailing and maritime trade, though the verse does not state this directly.

challenge.question: What striking linguistic detail appears in the verse?
challenge.explanation: The repeated coastal wording emphasizes Zebulun’s maritime location.

challenge.question: What does “his border shall be unto Zidon” describe?
answers: The edge of Zebulun’s territory toward Zidon
challenge.explanation: It describes the boundary of his territory in relation to Zidon.

questions.question: What is a reasonable inference from Zebulun’s being a haven of ships?
answers: He lived only in the mountains
He may have been connected with sailing and sea trade
He was forbidden to approach the sea
questions.explanation: A harbor could support sailing and maritime trade, though the verse does not state this directly.

questions.question: What striking linguistic detail appears in the verse?
questions.explanation: The repeated coastal wording emphasizes Zebulun’s maritime location.

questions.question: What does “his border shall be unto Zidon” describe?
answers: The edge of Zebulun’s territory toward Zidon
questions.explanation: It describes the boundary of his territory in relation to Zidon.

paragraphs.title: Issachar Works in a Good Land

easy.question: What animal is Issachar compared to?
easy.explanation: Issachar is compared to a strong ass.

easy.question: Between what does Issachar couch?
easy.explanation: The verse says he couches between two burdens.

easy.question: What did Issachar see was good?
easy.explanation: He saw that rest was good.

medium.question: What led Issachar to bow his shoulder to bear?
answers: He saw that the land was pleasant and rest was good
He wanted to leave the land
medium.explanation: Seeing the good land and rest led him to accept the burden.

medium.question: What does “tribute” mean here?
medium.explanation: The passage describes becoming subject to labor or tribute.

medium.question: What is the sequence in these verses?
answers: Issachar became a servant, then saw the land, then rested
He saw good rest and pleasant land, bowed his shoulder, and became a servant
He found an ass, left the land, and rested
medium.explanation: The verses present those three steps in that order.

challenge.question: What quality is emphasized by comparing Issachar to an ass?
answers: Strength and ability to bear a burden
challenge.explanation: The image emphasizes endurance and the ability to carry burdens.

challenge.question: What is the main tension in Issachar’s description?
answers: He enjoys good land but accepts work and burden because of it
He wants rest but must go to war
He receives bad land but refuses to work
challenge.explanation: The passage combines pleasant rest with the burden of labor.

challenge.question: What can we infer from “he saw” followed by “bowed his shoulder”?
answers: Seeing the land made him flee
Recognizing the land’s goodness influenced him to accept the work
He did not understand his situation
challenge.explanation: The sequence links his recognition of the land’s goodness to his decision to bear the burden.

questions.question: What quality is emphasized by comparing Issachar to an ass?
answers: Strength and ability to bear a burden
questions.explanation: The image emphasizes endurance and the ability to carry burdens.

questions.question: What is the main tension in Issachar’s description?
answers: He enjoys good land but accepts work and burden because of it
He wants rest but must go to war
He receives bad land but refuses to work
questions.explanation: The passage combines pleasant rest with the burden of labor.

questions.question: What can we infer from “he saw” followed by “bowed his shoulder”?
answers: Seeing the land made him flee
Recognizing the land’s goodness influenced him to accept the work
He did not understand his situation
questions.explanation: The sequence links his recognition of the land’s goodness to his decision to bear the burden.

easy.question: What will Dan do?
easy.explanation: The verse says Dan shall judge his people.

easy.question: What animal appears in verse 17?
easy.explanation: Dan is compared to a serpent and an adder.

easy.question: From whom does Jacob await salvation?
easy.explanation: Jacob says, “I have waited for thy salvation, O Lord.”

medium.question: What causes the rider to fall backward?
answers: The serpent bites the horse’s heels
The horse stops by the road
medium.explanation: The serpent bites the horse’s heels, causing the rider to fall.

medium.question: What is an adder in the path?
answers: A person walking on the road
medium.explanation: The verse describes a snake lying in wait along the path.

medium.question: What does “as one of the tribes of Israel” show about Dan?
answers: Dan does not belong to Israel
Dan is recognized as one of Israel’s tribes
medium.explanation: The phrase places Dan among the tribes of Israel.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the serpent biting the horse’s heels?
answers: A small hidden creature can bring down a greater power
Horses are always protected from snakes
challenge.explanation: The small serpent causes the rider to fall, showing the power of a hidden threat.

challenge.question: What is the sequence in verse 17?
answers: The rider falls, then the serpent reaches the path
The serpent bites the horse, then the rider falls backward
The horse falls, then the rider bites the serpent
challenge.explanation: The bite comes before the rider’s fall.

challenge.question: What does the movement from Dan’s description to Jacob’s prayer suggest?
answers: Jacob stops discussing Dan and blesses the horse
Alongside Dan’s strength, Jacob expresses hope in God’s salvation
challenge.explanation: The passage turns from Dan’s striking image to dependence on the Lord.

questions.question: What can we infer from the serpent biting the horse’s heels?
answers: A small hidden creature can bring down a greater power
Horses are always protected from snakes
questions.explanation: The small serpent causes the rider to fall, showing the power of a hidden threat.

questions.question: What is the sequence in verse 17?
answers: The rider falls, then the serpent reaches the path
The serpent bites the horse, then the rider falls backward
The horse falls, then the rider bites the serpent
questions.explanation: The bite comes before the rider’s fall.

questions.question: What does the movement from Dan’s description to Jacob’s prayer suggest?
answers: Jacob stops discussing Dan and blesses the horse
Alongside Dan’s strength, Jacob expresses hope in God’s salvation
questions.explanation: The passage turns from Dan’s striking image to dependence on the Lord.

easy.question: What is said about Gad?
answers: He will overcome his enemies at last
easy.explanation: Though attacked, Gad will overcome at the last.

easy.question: What will Asher provide?
easy.explanation: Asher will yield royal dainties.

easy.question: What is Naphtali compared to?
easy.explanation: Naphtali is compared to a hind let loose.

medium.question: What does Gad’s overcoming at the last mean?
answers: Gad will flee from the enemy
Gad will finally defeat his enemy
medium.explanation: The verse says Gad will overcome in the end.

medium.question: What does “fat” mean in “his bread shall be fat”?
medium.explanation: Here “fat” describes rich, plentiful food.

medium.question: What is the correct comparison of Asher and Naphtali?
answers: Asher is a warrior and Naphtali is a king
Asher is linked with rich food and Naphtali with beautiful words
Asher is a hind and Naphtali is a troop
medium.explanation: Asher is associated with food, while Naphtali is associated with a hind and goodly words.

challenge.question: What linguistic pattern stands out in the verse about Gad?
answers: Words from the same root for attacking recur
A comparison to a hind appears
challenge.explanation: The verse repeats related forms describing attack and overcoming.

challenge.question: What can we infer from rich bread and royal dainties?
answers: Asher does not use his food
Asher receives food only from the king
Asher has enough food to provide excellent delicacies
challenge.explanation: His abundance enables him to provide royal-quality food.

challenge.question: What combined idea appears in Naphtali’s description?
answers: Freedom or speed together with gracious speech
challenge.explanation: The released hind suggests freedom or speed, while goodly words suggest graceful speech.

questions.question: What linguistic pattern stands out in the verse about Gad?
answers: Words from the same root for attacking recur
A comparison to a hind appears
questions.explanation: The verse repeats related forms describing attack and overcoming.

questions.question: What can we infer from rich bread and royal dainties?
answers: Asher does not use his food
Asher receives food only from the king
Asher has enough food to provide excellent delicacies
questions.explanation: His abundance enables him to provide royal-quality food.

questions.question: What combined idea appears in Naphtali’s description?
answers: Freedom or speed together with gracious speech
questions.explanation: The released hind suggests freedom or speed, while goodly words suggest graceful speech.

paragraphs.title: Joseph, the Bow, and the Blessings

easy.question: To whom does “a fruitful bough” refer?
easy.explanation: The passage describes Joseph as a fruitful bough.

easy.question: Who grieved and shot at Joseph?
easy.explanation: The verse mentions the archers who shot at him.

easy.question: What blessings are mentioned?
answers: Blessings of heaven, the deep, the breasts, and the womb
easy.explanation: The passage lists blessings from heaven, the deep, and fertility.

medium.question: What happened after Joseph’s enemies attacked him?
answers: His bow remained strong and his arms were strengthened
medium.explanation: Despite their attacks, his bow remained strong and his arms were strengthened.

medium.question: What does “abode in strength” mean?
medium.explanation: The phrase says Joseph’s bow remained strong.

medium.question: What is said about Joseph’s father’s blessings?
answers: They surpassed the blessings of his ancestors and would endure
medium.explanation: Jacob says his blessings prevailed above those of his progenitors.

challenge.question: What might the branches running over the wall symbolize?
answers: A journey through a waterless desert
challenge.explanation: The spreading branches suggest overflowing growth and fruitfulness.

challenge.question: What do the titles “the God of thy father,” “the Almighty,” “the mighty God of Jacob,” and “the shepherd” have in common?
answers: They describe the source of divine help and protection
challenge.explanation: These titles present God as Joseph’s helper, protector, and shepherd.

challenge.question: What does “separate from his brethren” mean of Joseph?
answers: Joseph vowed not to drink wine
Joseph was distinguished and honored among his brothers
challenge.explanation: In this blessing, the phrase highlights Joseph’s special status.

questions.question: What might the branches running over the wall symbolize?
answers: A journey through a waterless desert
questions.explanation: The spreading branches suggest overflowing growth and fruitfulness.

questions.question: What do the titles “the God of thy father,” “the Almighty,” “the mighty God of Jacob,” and “the shepherd” have in common?
answers: They describe the source of divine help and protection
questions.explanation: These titles present God as Joseph’s helper, protector, and shepherd.

questions.question: What does “separate from his brethren” mean of Joseph?
answers: Joseph vowed not to drink wine
Joseph was distinguished and honored among his brothers
questions.explanation: In this blessing, the phrase highlights Joseph’s special status.

paragraphs.title: Benjamin and the Blessing of All the Tribes

easy.question: Which tribe is described as a wolf?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Benjamin shall ravin as a wolf.”

easy.question: What will the wolf devour in the morning?
easy.explanation: In the morning he will devour the prey.

easy.question: How many tribes are mentioned?
easy.explanation: The verse refers to the twelve tribes of Israel.

medium.question: What will happen at evening?
answers: The wolf will divide the spoil
medium.explanation: At night he will divide the spoil.

medium.question: What is “spoil”?
medium.explanation: Spoil is property taken after victory.

medium.question: How did Jacob bless the tribes?
answers: He gave everyone exactly the same blessing
He blessed each one according to his blessing
medium.explanation: Each tribe received a blessing suited to it.

challenge.question: What can we infer from morning devouring and evening dividing the spoil?
answers: The wolf first obtains prey and then distributes it
The wolf acts only at night
challenge.explanation: The verse presents obtaining prey first and distributing it later.

challenge.question: What does “all these” at the start of verse 28 refer to?
challenge.explanation: It summarizes Jacob’s words about all the tribes.

challenge.question: What central idea comes from blessing each tribe according to its blessing?
answers: All tribes had the same character and role
The blessings concerned only the past
Each tribe had its own distinctive blessing and character
challenge.explanation: Jacob’s blessings were individually suited to the tribes.

questions.question: What can we infer from morning devouring and evening dividing the spoil?
answers: The wolf first obtains prey and then distributes it
The wolf acts only at night
questions.explanation: The verse presents obtaining prey first and distributing it later.

questions.question: What does “all these” at the start of verse 28 refer to?
questions.explanation: It summarizes Jacob’s words about all the tribes.

questions.question: What central idea comes from blessing each tribe according to its blessing?
answers: All tribes had the same character and role
The blessings concerned only the past
Each tribe had its own distinctive blessing and character
questions.explanation: Jacob’s blessings were individually suited to the tribes.

paragraphs.title: Jacob’s Charge and Burial in Machpelah

easy.question: To whom did Jacob give these instructions?
easy.explanation: Jacob charged his sons.

easy.question: Where did Jacob ask to be buried?
answers: In the cave in the field of Machpelah
easy.explanation: He asked to be buried in the cave of Machpelah.

easy.question: Who bought the field and the cave?
easy.explanation: Abraham bought them from Ephron the Hittite.

medium.question: Why does Jacob identify the cave and its former owners?
answers: To identify his burial place clearly
To tell where he was born
medium.explanation: The details identify the burial place precisely.

medium.question: What happened before Jacob asked to be buried there?
answers: Ephron sold the cave to Joseph
Abraham bought the field from Ephron
Isaac bought the field from Mamre
medium.explanation: Abraham had purchased the field and cave from Ephron.

medium.question: What does “I am to be gathered unto my people” mean?
answers: I am about to die and join my ancestors
medium.explanation: The context of burial with his fathers indicates death.

challenge.question: What can we understand from “with my fathers” and Jacob’s burial request?
answers: Jacob wants to be buried with his family and ancestors
Jacob wants to live with his ancestors
Jacob wants to build a new city
challenge.explanation: Jacob asks to join his ancestors in burial.

challenge.question: What geographical detail is given about the cave?
answers: It is before Mamre in the land of Canaan
challenge.explanation: The passage places it before Mamre in Canaan.

challenge.question: What does “for a possession of a buryingplace” mean?
challenge.explanation: The field was purchased as a burial possession.

questions.question: What can we understand from “with my fathers” and Jacob’s burial request?
answers: Jacob wants to be buried with his family and ancestors
Jacob wants to live with his ancestors
Jacob wants to build a new city
questions.explanation: Jacob asks to join his ancestors in burial.

questions.question: What geographical detail is given about the cave?
answers: It is before Mamre in the land of Canaan
questions.explanation: The passage places it before Mamre in Canaan.

questions.question: What does “for a possession of a buryingplace” mean?
questions.explanation: The field was purchased as a burial possession.

paragraphs.title: Machpelah: The Burial Place of the Patriarchs and Matriarchs

easy.question: Whom did they bury there?
easy.explanation: The verse says Abraham and Sarah were buried there.

easy.question: Who was Sarah?
easy.explanation: Sarah is called Abraham’s wife.

easy.question: Whom does the speaker say he buried?
easy.explanation: The verse ends, “there I buried Leah.”

medium.question: Which other couple is mentioned as buried there?
medium.explanation: The verse also mentions Isaac and Rebekah.

medium.question: What does “there” mean in “There they buried Abraham”?
medium.explanation: It refers to the burial place being discussed.

medium.question: Who is mentioned after Abraham and Sarah?
medium.explanation: The verse next names Isaac and Rebekah.

challenge.question: What can we infer from “there they buried” versus “there I buried”?
answers: The speaker says that he personally buried Leah
challenge.explanation: “I buried” is first person and indicates the speaker’s personal action.

challenge.question: What do the first two couples have in common?
answers: Each couple consists of a husband and wife
challenge.explanation: The verse names Abraham with Sarah and Isaac with Rebekah.

challenge.question: Which detail is not explicitly stated in the verse?
answers: Isaac and Rebekah were buried there
The name of the burial place
challenge.explanation: The verse says “there” but does not name the place.

questions.question: What can we infer from “there they buried” versus “there I buried”?
answers: The speaker says that he personally buried Leah
questions.explanation: “I buried” is first person and indicates the speaker’s personal action.

questions.question: What do the first two couples have in common?
answers: Each couple consists of a husband and wife
questions.explanation: The verse names Abraham with Sarah and Isaac with Rebekah.

questions.question: Which detail is not explicitly stated in the verse?
answers: Isaac and Rebekah were buried there
The name of the burial place
questions.explanation: The verse says “there” but does not name the place.

paragraphs.title: The Field and Cave Bought from the Hittites

easy.question: What is mentioned in the verse?
easy.explanation: The verse mentions the purchase of the field and cave.

easy.question: From whom were the field and cave bought?
easy.explanation: They were bought from the children of Heth.

easy.question: What was in the field?
easy.explanation: The verse refers to the cave that was in the field.

medium.question: What does “the purchase of the field and of the cave” mean?
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to property that was purchased.

medium.question: What connects the field and the cave?
answers: The cave is in the city
The cave is in the field
The field is inside the cave
medium.explanation: The verse says the cave is in the field.

medium.question: What can we understand from their being bought from the children of Heth?
answers: They were property acquired in a transaction
They were gifts with no owner
They were found in the wilderness
medium.explanation: The verse describes a purchase from the Hittites.
